title: Indian-Origin Man Gurmeet Singh Stripped of US Citizenship Over Concealed Rape Conviction
excerpt: A federal court in Brooklyn revoked the naturalization of Gurmeet Singh, a convicted rapist serving 20 years, who concealed his crimes during the citizenship process.
body:
• The US District Court for the Eastern District of New York revoked the naturalization of Indian-born Gurmeet Singh, 55, who concealed a rape and kidnapping during his citizenship application.
  • Singh, a former taxi driver, was convicted in 2014 of first-degree rape and second-degree kidnapping and is serving a 20-year sentence at Shawangunk Correctional Facility in New York.
  • He must surrender his naturalization certificate and US passport by September 16 and faces possible deportation upon release in February 2029.
  • The case is part of a broader Justice Department push to denaturalize hundreds of convicted criminals who obtained citizenship through fraud.

A federal court in Brooklyn has revoked the US citizenship of Indian-born Gurmeet Singh, a convicted rapist who concealed his crimes while applying for naturalization more than a decade ago, the Department of Justice announced on Monday.

The US District Court for the Eastern District of New York entered judgment stripping Singh, 55, of his naturalized citizenship following an August 26 order by Judge Nicholas Garaufis. Singh has been ordered to surrender his naturalization certificate and US passport by September 16.

The Crime and Cover-Up

According to the DOJ complaint, Singh was working as a taxi driver in New York in May 2011 when he drove a female passenger who had fallen asleep during her ride from Williamsburg to her East Village apartment. He took her to a secluded location, and the woman awoke to find Singh on top of her with a knife to her throat. He bound and gagged her, blindfolded her, and raped her before the victim managed to escape and seek help from a passerby at dawn.

https://x.com/nicksortor/status/2094492363326382341

Just weeks after the assault, Singh filed his application to naturalize as a US citizen. He concealed the pending criminal case throughout the naturalization proceedings and was granted citizenship on October 19, 2011.

Singh was subsequently convicted in May 2014 in New York of Rape in the First Degree and Kidnapping in the Second Degree as a Sexually Motivated Felony. He was sentenced to 20 years in prison and is currently incarcerated at Shawangunk Correctional Facility in Ulster County, New York.

A Broader Denaturalization Push

The case is part of a significantly expanded denaturalization effort by the Justice Department under the Trump administration. Updated guidance from the department in late 2025 directed US Citizenship and Immigration Services to present 100 to 200 denaturalization cases per month in fiscal year 2026 — a dramatic increase from the historical average of roughly 11 cases per year between 1990 and 2017, according to the Washington Times.

"American citizenship is not a shield for criminals. Gurmeet Singh, a convicted rapist from India, is no longer a U.S. citizen. Fraudulently obtained citizenship will not protect criminals from justice."

— Todd Blanche, US Attorney General

Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate of the Justice Department's Civil Division said Singh "unlawfully obtained the privileges of US citizenship by concealing horrible criminal acts" and vowed the department would "continue to protect the integrity of the citizenship process."

Singh's Immigration History

Singh entered the United States in February 1992 on a temporary visitor visa that allowed him to stay for six months. He overstayed for years without authorization before a family-based immigrant visa petition enabled him to become a permanent resident in June 2000. He then applied for and obtained citizenship in 2011 while concealing an active criminal case.

The denaturalization complaint was filed by the Justice Department on February 2, 2026, and the court entered judgment less than seven months later.

What Comes Next

Singh is scheduled for release from prison in February 2029. Following his release, the Department of Homeland Security will determine whether to initiate deportation proceedings. With his citizenship now revoked, Singh has no legal protection against removal from the United States.

The case was prosecuted by Trial Attorney Christopher Lyerla of the Civil Division's Office of Immigration Litigation and Assistant US Attorney Layaliza Soloveichik for the Eastern District of New York.

For the Indian diaspora community in the US, the case underscores the serious consequences of misrepresentation during the naturalization process and comes amid heightened scrutiny of immigration fraud under current Justice Department priorities.
